# Pear scripting

Pear is an outdoor, social, mixed-reality platform: phones (GPS, motion, haptics), AirPods and watches replace screens. Prefer games played in the real world (tag, manhunt, capture the flag) over screen games.

Scripts are plain JavaScript in `/scripts/`. You may also read and write any other file in the project.

- `scripts/<name>.client.js` is a **client script** (runs per player, attached to an entity).
- `scripts/<name>.server.js` is a **server script** (runs once per room, never sees input).
- Through Pear MCP the same files are `scripts/client/<name>.js` and `scripts/server/<name>.js`.

The file must begin with `export default` as its very first characters (no leading comments or blank lines; the engine only rewrites sources starting with it, so put comments inside the IIFE); keep helpers and state inside an IIFE. `script` and `serverScript` are globals (no imports).

```js
export default (function () {
  return script({
    onLookAt(self, ctx) { ctx.remote.fire("tag", { tag: "seen" }); },
  });
})();
```

Unknown handler names or non-function values throw a TypeError at load. One client script context may serve several entities: key per-entity state by `self.name`.

## Client: `script({...})`, handlers get `(self, ctx, ...args)`

- `onLookAt(self, ctx)`: The head ray has stayed on this entity for 0.5 s.
- `onGesture(self, ctx, g)`: A gesture arrived from any device. type is a built-in gesture or the name of a scene motion gesture (scene.gestures). flick and motion gestures carry dir. "raise" and "lower" come only when the scene has gestures.raise: the device tilted away from (raise) or back toward (lower) its rest pose; they carry g.t, the time of the device packet that crossed.
- `onHeartRate(self, ctx, bpm)`: Heart rate changed. ctx.intensity is the normalized 0..1 value.
- `onRaycastHit(self, ctx)`: The aim ray hit this entity.
- `onTriggerEnter(self, ctx)`: The player entered this entity's trigger volume.
- `onTriggerExit(self, ctx)`: The player left this entity's trigger volume.
- `onRemote(self, ctx, name, data)`: The server sent this player a remote event.
- `onTick(self, ctx, dt)`: Runs 5 times a second. dt is seconds since the last tick.

Members:

- `self.name: string`: Name of the entity this script is attached to.
- `self.speed: number`: Speed multiplier for this entity. Read and write.
- `self.position: [x, y, z]`: Entity position in meters. Reading it works; writes have no effect.
- `self.audio.play(sound: string)`: Plays a built-in sound in the Studio. Built-in sounds: "beep". An unknown name logs a warning in the browser console and plays nothing.
- `self.audio.stop()`: Stops the sound and any speech that is playing.
- `self.audio.speak(text: string)`: Speaks the text aloud with the browser's speech synthesis. Does nothing where speech is unavailable.
- `self.calibrate()`: Makes this player's current device orientation the rest pose that gestures.raise measures from. Call it when the player holds the device in their starting position.
- `ctx.intensity: number`: Normalized heart rate, 0..1. Set on heart-rate calls.
- `ctx.player.id: string | null`: This player's id from the game server; null until the server welcome arrives.
- `ctx.player.role: "player" | "ref"`: The role picked for this player in the Studio Test panel (Add player: Player or Referee; your own player defaults to "player" and can be switched). Test-only: the game decides what it means, e.g. send its own "role" remote event. "player" when nothing was picked.
- `ctx.positionAccuracy: number | null`: Horizontal accuracy of ctx.position in meters. null without the location permission or a fix.
- `ctx.position: [x, y, z] | null`: This player's position. Only set when scene.permissions.location is true, else null.
- `ctx.remote.fire(name: string, data?: any)`: Sends a remote event to the server. The only way off the client.
- `ctx.spawn(name: string)`: Asks the runtime to spawn an entity. Not simulated in local runs.
- `ctx.haptic(pattern: string, intensity: number)`: Plays a haptic pattern on the player's device. Intensity 0..1.
- `console.log(...args)`: Writes to the Output tab. console.warn and console.error work too.

## Server: `serverScript({...})`, handlers get `(ctx, ...args)`

- `onPlayerJoin(ctx, player)`: A player joined the session.
- `onPlayerLeave(ctx, player)`: A player left the session.
- `onRemote(ctx, player, name, data)`: A client fired a remote event.
- `onTimer(ctx, tag, data)`: A timer set with ctx.after fired.

Members:

- `ctx.state: object`: Plain object that lives in the hosted session. Resets when a new version is published.
- `ctx.remote.fire(playerId: string, name: string, data?: any)`: Sends a remote event to one player.
- `ctx.remote.fireAll(name: string, data?: any)`: Sends a remote event to every player.
- `ctx.now(): number`: Current time in milliseconds.
- `ctx.after(ms: number, tag: string, data?: any): number`: Fires onTimer after 50 ms to 1 h; at most 64 pending. Returns an id for ctx.cancel.
- `ctx.cancel(id: number)`: Cancels a pending ctx.after timer.
- `ctx.agent.run(prompt: string): Promise<string>`: Asks the hosted game agent and resolves with its reply. Server scripts only. Needs the hosted runtime: the backend must set PEAR_RUNTIME_SECRET plus the operator key env PEAR_GAME_AGENT_PROVIDER and PEAR_GAME_AGENT_KEY (operator-paid, the game never sees the key). Limits: 4000-character prompt, 10 calls per minute per game, 20 s timeout. Rejects with Error "agent runtime not configured" (any env missing, and always in Studio local runs), "agent prompt too long (max 4000 characters)", "agent rate limit exceeded (max 10 calls per minute per game)" or "agent timed out after 20s".
- `console.log(...args)`: Writes to the Server tab. console.warn and console.error work too.

Put the player id in the payload when sending to all.

## RemoteEvents

Client and server talk only through named events: client `ctx.remote.fire(name, data)` reaches the server `onRemote`; the server's `fireAll(name, data)` reaches every client `onRemote`, and `fire(playerId, name, data)` reaches one. Payloads are plain JSON.

## Limits and sandbox

- A client handler is stopped after 250 ms (watchdog); the error appears in the Output tab.
- A server call gets 1 s of CPU and 32 MiB of memory.
- No `fetch`, DOM, timers or files. The network is reachable only through remote events.
- Client scripts never see raw USIS packets; the server never sees input, only what clients send in remote events.
- `ctx.state` lives in the hosted session and resets when a new version is published.
- Gestures: `tap`, `doubleTap`, `flick` (with `dir`), `squeeze`, `pinch`.

## USIS v1 packets (what the device handlers are fed)

One packet per device sample, only changed channels present:
`{ v: 1, deviceId, kind, slot, source: "live"|"sim", t (ms), seq, ch: {...} }`

- `kind`: phone, tablet, airpods, watch, pencil, headset, custom. `slot`: head, leftWrist, rightWrist, hand, pocket, stylus.
- `ch.orientation` `[x,y,z,w]` unit quaternion; `ch.position`, `ch.accel` `[x,y,z]`. Frame: +X right, +Y up, -Z forward.
- `ch.touch` `[{id, x, y (0..1), phase: began|moved|ended}]`; `ch.gesture` `{type, dir?}`; `ch.heartRate` bpm; `ch.pencil` `{tip, pressure, roll, hover}`.

## Scene (`/scene.json`)

One JSON object. Axes: +X right, +Y up, -Z forward; meters.
- Scene fields: `name`, `requiredTier` (1-3), `playerOrigin` [x,y,z], `runMode` (`screen` | `device`), `permissions` (`{"location": true}` lets clients read `ctx.position`),
  `inputs` (`{head, position, heartRate, gestures: [...], players: [min, max]}`; Studio builds the simulated devices from it),
  `gestures` (motion gestures `{"name": {slot, axis, threshold, cooldownMs}}`, delivered as `onGesture` type `name`; plus `raise: {angleDeg: 80, hysteresisDeg: 10}`, defaults 80/10), `entities`. Leave `clientScripts` / `serverScripts` alone: the Studio fills them from the script files.
- Entity: `name` (unique among its siblings), `position` [x,y,z], `rotation` quaternion [x,y,z,w], `scale` [x,y,z],
  `shape` (`box` default or `sphere`), `color` (CSS colour), `children`, `components`.
- Components: `{"type":"script","name":"<client script>"}`; `{"type":"trigger","shape":"sphere","radius":1}` or
  `{"type":"trigger","shape":"box","size":[x,y,z]}`; `{"type":"audioEmitter","soundName":"...","gain":1,"loops":false}`.
- Entities are fixed in the scene file; `ctx.spawn` is not simulated in local runs, so add entities here instead.

## Manifest (`pear-game.json`, format `pear-game/1`)

Optional keys: `format`, `name`, `scene`, `scripts`, `players`, `capabilities`, `controller`, `cues`, `instructions`, `checks`. Sensors a game may ask for: `head`, `position`, `heartRate`, `motion`. Raise defaults 80/10 degrees. Leave `sensors` empty for location games (the backend rejects `location` there; use scene `permissions.location` instead).

## PearUI, scenarios and location games (from the Pear MCP kit reference)

```text
PEARUI v1 (ui.json): server-driven native UI; the same JSON renders on iOS and web
  {"pearui":1,"route":[{"when":"<expr>","screen":"<id>"},...,{"screen":"<id>"}],"screens":{"<id>":Node}}
  First matching route wins; the last route has no "when".
  View state (read-only): ev.<name> = latest data of each server->client event (ctx.remote.fireAll("state",d) gives ev.state);
    me = {id,name,lobby}; local.<k> = values set by "set" actions; device = {kind:"phone"|"ipad"|"watch"}.
  Bindings: any string prop may hold {{expr}}. expr = dotted path, optional == / != literal, ! prefix, || fallback, .length (arrays/strings, iOS). No JS.
  Equality is loose between number and string (2 == '2').
  Node common props: type, if(expr), id, style{tone:neutral|accent|good|bad|warn, size:s|m|l|xl|huge, align:start|center|end, pad:0-4, grow:bool}
  Nodes: column|row|stack(children) text(value) button(label,action) image(src=asset name) timer(until=epoch ms expr, counts down)
    list(items=expr->array, item=Node, inside it item.<k>) gauge(value 0..1) spacer map(markers=[{lat,lng,label,tone}], follow:"me")
    sensor(invisible; kind:motion|location; event; hz<=30; streams {pitch,roll,yaw} or {lat,lng,acc} to the server as that event)
    effect(invisible; on=expr change -> haptic:light|heavy|success|fail, sound:asset name)
  Action: {"send":"<event>","data":{...bindings}} or {"set":"<local key>","value":...}. Unknown node types render nothing.
  A PearUI client sends {"name":"role","data":{"role":"referee"|"phone","kind":"ipad"|"phone"}} on socket open. Scripts that ignore role are unaffected.
  Clients have no logic: a motion sensor streams "aim" {pitch,roll,yaw}; the server script does any thresholding/hysteresis.
  Aim pattern: put a sensor(kind:motion,event:"aim") on the phone screen; the server script reads "aim" and fires when pitch/roll cross its threshold, then fireAll("fire",{round}).
  Worked example (trimmed from Games/QuickDraw/ui.json):
    {"pearui":1,"route":[{"when":"device.kind == 'ipad'","screen":"referee"},{"screen":"gun"}],
     "screens":{
      "referee":{"type":"column","children":[
        {"type":"list","items":"ev.view.players","item":{"type":"row","children":[
          {"type":"text","value":"{{item.name}}"},{"type":"spacer"},{"type":"text","value":"{{item.score}}","style":{"size":"xl","tone":"accent"}}]}}]},
      "gun":{"type":"column","children":[
        {"type":"sensor","kind":"motion","event":"aim","hz":20,"id":"aim"},
        {"type":"effect","id":"fire-haptic","on":"ev.fire.round","haptic":"heavy"},
        {"type":"text","value":"{{ev.state.needs}}","if":"ev.view.players.length"},
        {"type":"button","label":"Ready","action":{"send":"ready","data":{"round":"{{ev.state.round}}"}},"if":"!ev.state.ready","style":{"tone":"accent"}}]}}}

  Location game (Manhunt-style): client streams {lat,lng,acc} via a location sensor; the server script does the distance maths.
    ui: {"type":"column","children":[
      {"type":"sensor","kind":"location","event":"location","hz":1,"id":"gps"},
      {"type":"map","markers":"ev.view.markers","follow":"me"},
      {"type":"text","value":"{{ev.view.hint}}"},
      {"type":"button","label":"Tag","action":{"send":"tag"},"if":"ev.view.role == 'hunter'"},
      {"type":"effect","id":"near","on":"ev.view.hint","haptic":"heavy"}]}
    server (JS): const R=6371000,rad=d=>d*Math.PI/180;
      const haversine=(a,b)=>{const h=Math.sin(rad(b.lat-a.lat)/2)**2+Math.cos(rad(a.lat))*Math.cos(rad(b.lat))*Math.sin(rad(b.lng-a.lng)/2)**2;return 2*R*Math.asin(Math.sqrt(h))};
      on "location" {lat,lng,acc}: store per player; hint = d<15?"Tag range":d<50?"Close":"Cold" (d metres to nearest runner); on "tag" accept only if haversine<=15.
    Markers are [{lat,lng,label,tone}] (tone good=green, bad=red, else orange). One location stream per screen.

SCENARIO (run_scenario: headless, real sockets against the hosted server)
  {"game":"<id>","version"?:n,"lobby"?:"CODE","durationMs":n,
   "devices":[{"name","kind":"phone"|"ipad"|"watch","role"?,
     "script":[{"at":ms,"send":{"name","data"}}|{"at":ms,"motion":{pitch,roll,yaw}}|{"at":ms,"gps":{lat,lng}}|{"at":ms,"tap":true}],
     "rules":[{"on":"<event>","when"?:"<expr over {data, ...viewState}>","after"?:ms,"send":{"name","data"},"once"?:bool}]}],
   "expect":[{"by":ms,"expr":"<expr on a device's view state>","device":"<name>"}]}
  Reactive rules answer server events (cues arrive at random times); {{expr}} in a rule's send.data resolves against {data, ...viewState}.
  Timed motion/gps steps send "aim"/"location" (override with scenario motionEvent / gpsEvent). A device role sends role {role} after _welcome.
  Report: {"ok","expect":[{...,"pass","actual"}],"frames":[{t,device,dir,name,data}],"logs":[],"final":{device:viewState}}.
  The scenario runs against the LATEST saved version unless "version" is set. Logs need an owner/developer token.
  Loop: save_version -> run_scenario -> read the report -> fix -> repeat until ok is true; then publish (publish = list: sets listed:true; optional description/tags/releaseNotes).
```

## Scaffolds (copy and adapt; generated from Games/)

- `scaffolds/QuickDraw/`: check.json, pear-game.json, scenario.json, scene.json, scripts/game.js, scripts/player.js, ui.json
- `scaffolds/HotPotato/`: check.json, scene.json, scripts/game.js, scripts/player.js
- `scaffolds/Manhunt/`: pear-game.json, scenario.json, scene.json, scripts/game.js, scripts/player.js, ui.json

Start from the nearest one: Manhunt for GPS games, Hot Potato for passing/tag, Quick Draw for motion reflex duels.

## Workflow

Read `/AGENTS.md` for the current scene, scripts and peripherals. Write small scripts, one per behaviour; use `edit_file` to change existing ones. Validate, run the headless scenario or pear-check, read the report, fix, repeat before saying done.

Model: the runtime uses Anthropic, OpenAI or Google Gemini, chosen by `PEAR_AGENT_MODEL` ("provider:model") or the first of `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`/`GEMINI_API_KEY` that is set.
